verdict.rationale: Appwrite ships an official MCP server, including a hosted version bundled in Claude Code and Codex plugins behind one OAuth sign-in. The docs say it lets AI tools such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Claude Desktop operate on an Appwrite project, so users can manage their backend through natural-language prompts in those agents. Missing for 10: a native natural-language interface inside Appwrite's own console, documented scope or limits of which operations work through natural language, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Appwrite offers a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that allows LLMs to directly interact with Appwrite's API and docs.
Using the MCP server, you can use applications such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Claude Desktop, and others to operate on your Appwrite project
The Appwrite plugins for Claude Code and Codex now include the hosted Appwrite MCP server, so your agent can work with your Appwrite project after one OAuth sign-in.
